d: Tumor suppressor genes whose proteins repair double-strand DNA breaks by homologous recombination. Inherited mutations raise breast and ovarian cancer risk, and BRCA2 also raises male breast cancer risk.
Contractile cells in the outer layer of breast ducts and lobules, resting on the basement membrane. They persist around carcinoma in situ and are lost once the cancer invades.
A calcium-dependent adhesion protein, encoded by CDH1, that holds epithelial cells together. Its loss makes lobular carcinoma cells loosely attached, so they grow in single file.
A receptor tyrosine kinase encoded by ERBB2. When the gene is amplified, HER2 drives growth signaling in HER2-positive breast cancer and makes the tumor a target for trastuzumab and related drugs.
A crusted, eczema-like nipple lesion caused by carcinoma cells that spread into the epidermis from an underlying DCIS or invasive carcinoma.
